body:
## Problem

- An alert owner whose AI detector check failed is told PostHog could not reach its model provider, whatever actually happened, and is then told the alert and insight settings are correct.
- `LLMDetectorUnavailableError` covers four distinct outcomes; only one is a provider failure.

| Raised where | What happened | Old message said |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `llm_detector_limits.py` | Rollout flag lookup returned nothing | Could not reach model provider |
| `judge/llm.py` slot acquire | Worker's model-call slots all busy | Could not reach model provider |
| `judge/llm.py` invoke | Provider transport failure | Could not reach model provider |
| `judge/llm.py` parse | Model reply unreadable | Could not reach model provider |

- The "settings are correct" line is asserted on a path that never reads those settings. In the rollout case it is wrong.
- `posthog_insight_alerts_ai_detector_checks_total{outcome="unavailable"}` counts once per Temporal attempt, not once per scheduled check. A check that retried four times reports four failures, and a retry that then succeeded reports both a failure and a success.
- `CheckAlertWorkflow` picks the evaluate task queue during prepare, but `evaluate_alert` reloads the alert. A detector-type edit in between sends the check to a worker that holds no model credentials.

Refs [#105367](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/105367)

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0cf7c-7b78-7992-8da0-4530bed648fa -->
## Origin

- Issues: [#105367](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/105367)
- First signal: 2026-09-23
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0cf7c-7b78-7992-8da0-4530bed648fa)
- Likely cause: [`227f42e`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/227f42ef5df08f079b7df010e19df0532d33b227)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0cf7c-7b78-7992-8da0-4530bed648fa -->

## Changes

- **Copy names the outcome, not a cause.** `LLM_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE`, the error email, and the in-app body now say the detector could not complete the check. The unverified "settings are correct" claim is gone from both surfaces. The email template context key follows: `provider_unavailable` becomes `detector_unavailable`.
- **The counter moves to the retry-exhausted path.** `record_failed_evaluation` increments `unavailable` when it actually writes an errored check; `evaluate_alert` no longer increments per attempt. One scheduled check is now one increment, and a retry that succeeds counts only `evaluated`.
- **`evaluate_alert` refuses a snapshot its queue cannot serve.** It compares the reloaded detector type against the type prepare routed on. On disagreement it returns no check and leaves `next_check_at` alone, so the next scheduler tick prepares and routes it again — the same skip the existing fingerprint guard already produces.
- Mechanical: test assertions and one parametrize id follow the renamed context key and the new wording.

> [!NOTE]
> Owner-facing wording changes for anyone already using the detector. No users are affected today — the feature is still behind its rollout flag.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only; the detector was not exercised against a live model.

New tests and the regression each catches:

- `test_skips_when_the_detector_type_no_longer_matches_the_routed_queue` — a check whose detector type changed after prepare would previously run on the wrong worker. Nothing covered the mismatch; the neighbouring snapshot test only changes the config *after* the load.
- `test_an_unavailable_detector_is_not_counted_on_every_attempt` — pins that `evaluate_alert` no longer counts, which is what made the counter scale with Temporal attempts.
- `test_counts_one_unavailable_outcome_per_recorded_failure` — pins one increment per recorded failure, and none for a non-detector error type.
- `test_does_not_count_an_unavailable_outcome_it_never_recorded` — a mid-check disable writes no errored check, so it must not move the counter either.
- Updated copy assertions now check the absence of the provider claim and the settings claim, not just their replacement.

Ran locally: `posthog/temporal/tests/test_alerts_activities.py`, `posthog/temporal/tests/test_alerts_workflows.py`, `products/alerts/backend/test/test_llm_judge.py`, `products/alerts/backend/test/test_email_notifications.py`, `products/alerts/backend/tests/api/test_alert.py`.

Not checked: the rendered email in a mail client, and any Temporal worker run against a real queue.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

The AI detector itself sits behind a rollout flag, so nothing here reaches users yet. The change adds no flag of its own.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None — no doc under `docs/` covers this copy or this metric.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

Duplicate check: `gh pr list --state open --search "ai detector alert unavailable"` returned ten open alerts PRs, none touching this error path, this counter, or the evaluate task queue.

Skills invoked: none of the mandatory triggers matched a code path here beyond copy and tests; `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments` and `/writing-pr-descriptions` shaped the wording, the test set, and this body.

CodeRabbit CLI: unavailable in this sandbox, so the PR opens without a local review pass.

Decisions along the way:

- The report offered outcome-based wording *or* a provider-specific exception subtype. Wording won: a subtype would need a second error code, a second serializer allowlist entry, and a second email branch, to tell the owner something they still cannot act on.
- Suppressing "Review the alert settings" for this code is kept. None of the four causes is the owner's to fix, so the advice would still be a dead end — only the claim that the settings *are correct* was unsupported.
- The queue guard returns the existing no-check skip rather than a new result shape, so `CheckAlertWorkflow` already reports it as `changed_during_evaluation` with no workflow change.
- One existing test passed a deliberately mismatched `uses_llm_detector` to prove the executor comes from the reloaded snapshot. The guard makes that input unreachable, so the test now passes the agreeing value and keeps its executor assertion.

Public artifact: the work drew only on this repository and the linked issue. No customer or session material is in the diff or this description.
